metadata.description: Curated IT / programming English vocabulary for the it-programming pack. ~60% real dictionary words with computing senses (enriched via dictionaryapi.dev with computing-sense preference), ~40% modern jargon with definition_en overrides. Informed by the Computer Science Word List (CSWL) and common 'English for IT' curricula.
metadata.cefr_note: cefr set only where the Oxford 5000 level is missing or wrong for the computing sense; default is B2.

terms.definition_en: to remove a program or application from a computer

not connected to the internet or a computer network

to join two or more strings or sequences end to end
the object-oriented principle of hiding an object's internal data behind a public interface
the object-oriented principle that the same operation can behave differently on different classes

the ability of a program to make progress on several tasks during the same period of time

a single document on the internet displayed in a browser
a program used to view websites, such as Chrome, Safari, or Firefox
the address of a web page, e.g. https://example.com (Uniform Resource Locator)

the language that describes how web pages look — colors, fonts, and layout (Cascading Style Sheets)
the programming language that makes web pages interactive, running in the browser
the part of a software system that users see and interact with, such as the pages of a website
the part of a software system users don't see — servers, databases, and application logic
covering both frontend and backend development; a full-stack developer works on both
a word, phrase, or image on a web page that you can click to go to another page
the first page a visitor arrives at, often designed to encourage one specific action

a window that appears suddenly on top of a web page, often showing an advertisement or message
to send a file from your device to a server or website
playing audio or video directly from the internet without downloading the whole file first
the box on a website or app where you type what you want to find
an application that runs in a web browser instead of being installed on a device
a lightweight text format for exchanging structured data between programs (JavaScript Object Notation)
a set of rules that lets one program request data or services from another (Application Programming Interface)

a screen that displays the most important information about a system or business in one view
to check that data is correct, complete, and in the expected format
presenting data as charts, graphs, or maps so patterns are easy to see
a plain-text file format where values are separated by commas, used to exchange tabular data (Comma-Separated Values)
a unit of digital information equal to about one billion bytes
a unit of digital information equal to about one thousand gigabytes
a situation where the same data was changed in two places and the system cannot decide which version to keep
(of data or processing) happening immediately, as events occur, without delay
the part of a computer that carries out instructions; the CPU
the central processing unit — the 'brain' of a computer that executes instructions
a processor specialized for graphics and parallel computation (Graphics Processing Unit)
a computer's fast, temporary working memory, cleared when the power is off (Random Access Memory)
the device inside a computer that stores data permanently
the main circuit board of a computer, connecting the processor, memory, and other components
a small camera connected to a computer, used for video calls
the standard connector for attaching devices like keyboards and drives to a computer (Universal Serial Bus)
an external device connected to a computer, such as a printer, keyboard, or mouse
permanent low-level software stored inside a hardware device that controls how it works
a screen you control by touching it with your fingers
a small portable device that plugs into a USB port and stores data
a fast storage device with no moving parts, commonly abbreviated SSD

a fan inside a computer that stops the processor and other parts from overheating
the maximum amount of data a network connection can carry per second

a device that connects computers to the internet and directs data between networks
the internet's address book, which translates domain names like example.com into IP addresses (Domain Name System)
the unique number that identifies a device on a network, e.g. 192.168.1.1
technology that connects devices to a network by radio instead of cables
the standard technology for connecting computers to a network with cables
to send a small test message to check whether a computer on a network responds, and how fast

a network of servers around the world that delivers web content from a location near each user (Content Delivery Network)
a service that creates a private, encrypted connection over the public internet (Virtual Private Network)
the state or quality of being connected to a network or the internet
a place or device that provides wifi internet access
a feature that lets an app keep working without an internet connection
(of a network) connecting computers directly to each other without a central server

the secure, encrypted version of HTTP, shown with a padlock in the browser
short-range wireless technology for connecting devices such as headphones and keyboards

converting data into a coded form so only authorized people can read it
to convert encrypted data back into its original readable form

malware that locks a victim's files and demands payment to unlock them
tricking people into revealing passwords or card details with fake emails or websites

continuously watching a system's health and performance to catch problems early
automatically recording events that happen in a system so problems can be investigated later

time when a system is not working or not available to users
a copy of the production environment where changes are tested before release
automatically building and testing code every time changes are pushed, so problems appear early
a system that spreads incoming traffic across several servers so no single one is overloaded
a small independent service that handles one business function and communicates with others over a network
a cloud model where the provider runs your code on demand and you never manage servers yourself
the amount of work a system completes in a given time, e.g. requests handled per second
automatically switching to a backup system when the main one fails

a plan showing what a product team intends to build and roughly when
the sequence of steps a piece of work goes through from start to finish

the field of AI that enables computers to understand images and video
